items.title: CBRE, North America Data Center Trends H1 2026
items.detail: 7,481 MW under construction across the eight US primary markets, up 24.8%. Vacancy 1.4%, net absorption 1,456 MW, over 80% of construction preleased.
items.effect: Hillsboro / Portland updated 430 to 491 MW, same source, newer vintage. The other seven markets keep their Knight Frank figures: CBRE counts primary-market colocation inventory, Knight Frank counts every operator's live IT capacity, so the gap is a population difference, not a discrepancy.

items.title: TCS / HyperVault, up to 1 GW in Telangana
items.detail: Up to Rs 70,000 crore, roughly $8.4bn, on 264 acres near Hyderabad, built in phases against customer demand. No completion date given.
items.effect: No change to today's figures. Announced capacity with no energization date is a claim, not load.

items.title: Vantage, Project Latigo, Laramie County, Wyoming
items.detail: Zone change approved unanimously. 480 MW across 1,835 acres, up to $20bn, with onsite generation, 12 miles south of Cheyenne.
items.effect: Not added. The campus layer comes from Epoch AI's dataset; a site enters when Epoch picks it up, because mixing news-sourced sites into a single-source layer breaks its provenance. A zoning approval is also permission, not load.

items.title: Epoch AI revises two campuses down
items.detail: Google New Albany cut from 453 to 333 MW and Meta Aiken from 142 to 69 MW in Epoch's frontier data centre dataset. Same source, newer estimate, no change of method.
items.effect: Mapped campus capacity 13,257 to 13,064 MW, down 193 MW, almost all of it US. Country and metro layers are unaffected: both sites sit outside a mapped metro, so nothing was double counted either way.

items.title: IEA publishes 485 TWh for 2025
items.detail: Key Questions on Energy and AI (16 April 2026) puts global data centre electricity at 485 TWh in 2025, up 17% on the year. The page is anchored to the IEA's 415 TWh for 2024, from Energy and AI.
items.effect: Not adopted, and the anchor is unchanged. The whole capacity basis here is IEA installed capacity for 2024 (122.2 GW); dividing 2025 energy by 2024 capacity would move kIea from 0.398 to 0.453 on a year mismatch rather than on evidence. It becomes adoptable when the IEA publishes a 2025 capacity figure to pair it with. Recorded in policy.json.

items.title: Oregon puts data centres in their own rate class
items.detail: The POWER Act (House Bill 3546, 2025) requires Oregon utilities to serve large energy use facilities of 20 MW and above under a separate schedule on contracts of ten years or longer. The PUC approved Portland General Electric's version in Order No. 26-239 on 10 July 2026, raising data centre rates about 29% on average while every other class fell. Pacific Power's is pending in Docket UE 463.
items.effect: No figure moved. Added to the regulatory set, where it attaches to Hillsboro / Portland — whose 491 MW (CBRE, H1 2026) is unchanged. Cost allocation is not generation, so no capacity or consumption value depends on it.

items.title: Pennsylvania sets a model large-load tariff
items.detail: PUC Final Order of 13 May 2026, Docket M-2025-3054271, adopted at the 30 April public meeting. It covers customers above 50 MW individually or 100 MW in aggregate: cost causation for interconnection, deposits and collateral against stranded cost, six-month study timelines, minimum contract terms and exit provisions, a public interconnection queue.
items.effect: No figure moved. Added to the regulatory set as a national-thread item; Pennsylvania has no mapped metro on this page, so nothing attaches to a marker. Found on a gap check rather than published this fortnight — it is here because the set had Ohio and Oregon but not the one statewide model tariff written for the same problem.

items.title: China's energy regulator: internet data services power use up 44%
items.detail: At its Jul 30, 2026 press conference the National Energy Administration reported that electricity used by the internet data services industry reached 49.4 billion kWh (49.4 TWh) in the first half of 2026, up 44% year on year. It is an official, measured series, but it counts consumption by enterprises classified as internet data services, a narrower and differently drawn population than the 260 TWh (2024) figure this page uses for China. Separately, a Wood Mackenzie projection of 774 TWh by 2030 (reported by China Daily, Sep 3, 2026) is a consultancy forecast and does not qualify under Test 1.
items.effect: No figure moved. China stays on 260 TWh (2024), scope mismatch declared. The NEA value is a half-year, 2026-vintage, industry-classified total, so it cannot be set against 2024 capacity, and it does not say whether telecom and 5G network rooms are in or out, which is the question that would settle China. Watching for a full-year NEA or CEC value.
items.src: National Energy Administration (China), press conference transcript, Jul 30, 2026

items.title: Pennsylvania opens a second data center proceeding
items.detail: At its Sep 10, 2026 public meeting the Pennsylvania PUC voted 5-0 to have staff propose updates to its emergency curtailment rules and hold a technical conference on cost allocation for data centers, with a tentative order due at the Oct 1, 2026 meeting and a final vote targeted for Jan 28, 2027. A companion motion set up a ratemaking working group (Docket M-2026-3064953). This follows the model large-load tariff (Docket M-2025-3054271) already in the regulatory set.
items.effect: No figure moved. Curtailment and cost allocation are not generation, and Pennsylvania has no mapped metro, so nothing attaches to a marker. The existing Pennsylvania entry is left as is until the tentative order is published with a docket number.

items.title: Eurostat publishes a measured data center electricity series
items.detail: Dataset isoc_env_ict_nrg, "Data centres' electricity consumption", last updated Jul 27, 2026, covering 2020-2024 in terajoules for 42 countries. The EU energy statistics regulation obliges member states to file data center energy use above 1 MW with Eurostat annually, colocation and enterprise alike, so this is measured national reporting rather than a consultancy model.
items.effect: No figure moved. The series reproduces three of the five anchors for 2024 within about 1% - Ireland 6.969 TWh against the CSO's 6.973, the Netherlands 5.093 against the CBS's 5.100, France 4.348 against SDES's 4.3 - which is independent corroboration of the metro basis rather than a new input. Germany is the live question and is recorded in policy.json: the series passes Test 1 there but fails Test 2 at 1.90. Finland, Poland and Spain would pass both tests, but admitting anchors moves kNat and needs calib.json, which this path will not carry.

items.title: Imperial Irrigation District adopts a curtail-first large load tariff
items.detail: The IID board voted unanimously on Sep 16, 2026 to adopt a Large Load Tariff for customers above 20 MW: infrastructure cost recovery, a minimum monthly charge of at least 85% of contracted energy, a fifteen-year commitment, cash deposits, and first place in line to be shut off when demand peaks.
items.effect: No figure moved, and it is not in the regulatory set. The tariff document on iid.com refused the request from here, so only the press account could be read, and that set holds filings read on the filing itself. Imperial Valley has no mapped metro, so nothing would attach to a marker either way. Recorded here so a later run can promote it once the document is reachable.

items.title: China Electricity Council: internet data services power use past 60 TWh this year
items.detail: At the 2026 Energy Green Development Conference, reported by CCTV News on Sep 16, 2026, the China Electricity Council said national electricity use by the internet data services industry has passed 60 billion kWh (60 TWh) so far in 2026, up more than 40% year on year and already far above the full-year 2024 level. It described the first half, the 49.4 TWh the National Energy Administration reported in July, as already close to that full-year 2024 total. The council's Pan Yuelong separately projected national computing-power electricity reaching 800 TWh by 2030, about 6% of all electricity used in China.
items.effect: No figure moved. China stays on 260 TWh (2024), scope mismatch declared. This is the same narrow industry classification as the National Energy Administration's half-year figure, it is a partial year, and it is 2026 vintage, so it cannot be set against 2024 capacity and Test 2 cannot be run on it at all. It does sharpen the mismatch rather than settle it: the council puts the full-year 2024 total for that classification close to 49.4 TWh, roughly a fifth of the 260 TWh this page uses for China in the same year, which is direct evidence the two sources count different populations. It still does not say whether telecom and 5G network rooms are inside the wider figure, which is the question that would settle China. The 800 TWh 2030 number is a projection and fails Test 1. The council's own site timed out from here, so this rests on the CCTV News account as carried by 21st Century Business Herald.
items.src: China Electricity Council, via CCTV News, Sep 16, 2026
